newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia gold output peak seen as costs rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia gold output peak seen as costs rise.

text.p: Australian gold production will continue to rise through to the end of the decade as miners bring new projects onstream and expand existing ones, the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) said on Tuesday.
But production would peak in about three years, as the cost of bringing new and less explored deposits on line caughts up with the industry, Simon Middleton, gold analyst for ABARE told Reuters.
ABARE has maintained its previous estimate that Australia will produce 303 tonnes of gold in 1996/97 (July/June), an 11 percent rise year-on-year.
Growth in production was unlikely to peak until 1999/2000, when production hits 336 tonnes, Middleton said.
He said growth in the Australian gold mining industry would come from mainly existing projects and new ones already on the drawing boards.

"Despite the prospect of significantly higher Australian gold production over the next few years, the rate of growth of the industry is projected to decline after 1999," Middleton said in a speech scheduled to be delivered on Wednesday to the ABARE commodities conference in Canberra.
"The Australian gold industry has now entered a period of declining profitability due to a declining real price of gold and increasing production costs," he said.
Over the next five years, operating cash costs were projected to climb to over A$380 an ounce, Middleton said.
"Costs of production are expected to increase because Australian gold production over the next five years will come increasingly from underground and deeper open cut operations," Middleton said.
